title: 8 Best Collections Software Tools in 2026
summary: Compare the 8 best collections software tools in 2026, from HighRadius and Billtrust to AI agents like Concourse, by automation depth, customer experience, and cost.
body_markdown:
Collections is where revenue you have already earned sits waiting. Chasing overdue invoices, sending reminder after reminder, deciding which accounts to call first, and logging every promise to pay is repetitive, relationship-sensitive work that scales badly as a company grows. Collections software exists to automate that follow-up: sequencing dunning, prioritizing the riskiest accounts, giving collectors a worklist, and tracking disputes so cash arrives sooner.


But "collections software" spans a wide range, from full order-to-cash suites like HighRadius and Billtrust to collaborative AR portals like Versapay, focused workflow tools like Gaviti, and the newer wave of AI agents that *do* the follow-up rather than give you a place to manage it. This guide compares the eight best collections software tools in 2026, so you can match the tool to your receivables, your customers, and your team.


## **What is the best collections software?**


> The best collections software in 2026 is Concourse for teams that want AI agents to run AR follow-up end to end, HighRadius for enterprise autonomous collections at scale, Billtrust for collections tied to invoicing and B2B payments, Versapay for collaborative customer-facing AR, Esker for collections inside a broad order-to-cash suite, Sidetrade for AI-driven collections intelligence, Quadient AR for growing mid-market teams, and Gaviti for fast-to-deploy collections workflows.


> **Concourse is the AI-agent option on this list.** Instead of a workflow tool you manage collections in, Concourse deploys autonomous finance agents that connect to your ERP, billing, and banking systems and run the follow-up itself, drafting and sending reminders, prioritizing the accounts most at risk, matching payments as they arrive, and flagging the accounts that need a human call, with every action traceable to source and a person approving.


## **How we evaluated collections software**


Collections tools are not interchangeable; a company with thousands of small invoices and one with a handful of large, relationship-driven accounts need very different things. We compared these across the criteria that change the decision:


- **Automation depth.** How much of the follow-up, dunning sequences, reminders, and escalation, runs automatically versus by hand.
- **Prioritization and intelligence.** Whether the tool ranks accounts by risk and predicts payment dates, so collectors work the right accounts first.
- **Customer experience.** Whether customers get a portal to view invoices, raise disputes, and pay, which affects how quickly they respond.
- **Order-to-cash breadth.** Whether collections is standalone or part of a suite that also covers invoicing, cash application, and credit.
- **ERP fit and integration.** How cleanly it connects to your accounting system and keeps AR data in sync.
- **AI capability.** From rules-based reminder sequences to AI agents that perform the follow-up.

## **The 8 best collections software tools in 2026**


### **1. Concourse, Best for AI Agents That Run AR Follow-Up**


Concourse is an AI agent platform for corporate finance. Rather than a workflow surface you manage collections in, it connects directly to your ERP, billing, and banking systems and runs the receivables follow-up itself: drafting and sending reminders on a cadence, prioritizing the accounts most likely to slip, matching incoming payments against open invoices, and flagging the accounts that need a human call.


What sets it apart from a collections workflow tool is the execution model. Concourse does not just track which accounts are overdue; its agents do the follow-up and the payment matching, and every action traces back to source data and is validated against evals built for your business, which is what makes the output defensible. It meets teams where they work, inside ChatGPT, Claude, Slack, Teams, and email, and connects to 100+ systems including NetSuite, QuickBooks, Snowflake, and Stripe. Concourse reports customer results including a 75% reduction in manual work and 20+ hours saved per user per month, and is SOC 2 Type II certified. See our guides to the[accounts receivable aging report](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/accounts-receivable-aging-report) and[cash application](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/cash-application) for how this fits the wider AR cycle.


**Best for.** Teams that want AI agents to actually perform AR follow-up and payment matching, with full traceability, rather than a tool to manage the process in.


**Keep in mind.** Concourse runs the collections work; it is not a customer-facing payment portal or a full order-to-cash billing suite. Many teams run Concourse for the follow-up and matching alongside an invoicing or payments tool.


### **2. HighRadius, Best for Enterprise Autonomous Collections**


HighRadius is an order-to-cash and treasury platform whose Autonomous Receivables suite uses AI to prioritize collector worklists, auto-send dunning correspondence, predict payment dates, and surface at-risk accounts, with deep ERP integration. Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Houston, it[raised a $300M round in 2021 at a valuation over $3 billion](https://www.highradius.com/about/news/highradius-raises-300m-series-c-at-over-3-billion-valuation/) .


**Best for.** Large enterprises with high-volume, complex AR that want autonomous, AI-driven collections at scale.


**Keep in mind.** It is built for large operations; implementation is a multi-month enterprise project and can be heavier and costlier than smaller teams need.


### **3. Billtrust, Best for Collections Tied to Invoicing and Payments**


Billtrust pairs collections workflows, automated reminders, collector task management, and dispute tracking, with invoice delivery and an integrated B2B payments network, so follow-up and getting paid live in one place. After going public in 2021, it was[taken private by EQT in 2022](https://eqtgroup.com/news/eqt-private-equity-to-acquire-billtrust-2022-09-28) (previously NASDAQ: BTRS).


**Best for.** Mid-market to enterprise teams that want collections alongside invoicing and payments in one platform.


**Keep in mind.** Much of its strength and pricing is tied to the payments and invoicing suite, so buyers wanting a pure standalone collections tool may pay for more than they use.


### **4. Versapay, Best for Collaborative Customer-Facing AR**


Versapay takes a collaborative approach to AR: a shared customer portal where buyers and your collectors resolve invoices, disputes, and short-pays in one thread, cutting the email back-and-forth behind aging follow-up. Founded in 2006, it was[acquired by Great Hill Partners in 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Versapay) and later added cash-application specialist DadeSystems.


**Best for.** Mid-market to enterprise teams whose collections bottleneck is customer communication and dispute resolution.


**Keep in mind.** The model works best when your customers actually adopt the portal; the value is lower if buyers will not engage through it.


### **5. Esker, Best for Collections Within Order-to-Cash**


Esker is a broad order-to-cash suite with a dedicated collections module, collection strategies, reminder cadences, a collector cockpit, and dispute handling, alongside credit, invoicing, and cash application. Founded in 1985 in Lyon, France, it was[taken private by Bridgepoint and General Atlantic in 2024](https://www.esker.com/company/press-releases/esker-and-bridgepoint-announce-proposed-cash-public-tender-offer-esker-shares/) .


**Best for.** Mid-market to enterprise teams that want collections as part of a wider order-to-cash deployment.


**Keep in mind.** Collections is one module in a large platform, often sold as part of a broader O2C project rather than a quick point solution.


### **6. Sidetrade, Best for AI Collections Intelligence**


Sidetrade is an AI-led order-to-cash platform whose "Aimie" engine drives collections prioritization, payment-date prediction, and automated dunning across large receivables ledgers, with particular strength in Europe. Founded in 2000, it is[publicly listed on Euronext Paris under ticker ALBFR](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/epa/ALBFR/company/) .


**Best for.** Mid-market to enterprise teams that want data-driven collections prioritization and payment prediction.


**Keep in mind.** It is a broad O2C intelligence platform; smaller teams may find it more than they need, and its North American footprint is younger than its European one.


### **7. Quadient AR (formerly YayPay), Best for Growing Mid-Market Teams**


Quadient AR, formerly YayPay, offers collections management with automated, escalating dunning workflows, a collector worklist, a customer payment portal, and AI-based payment predictions, well-suited to growing finance teams. YayPay was[acquired by Quadient and later rebranded as Quadient AR](https://www.quadient.com/en-int/news/quadient-announces-acquisition-leading-fintech-company-yaypay-specialized-accounts-receivable-automation) .


**Best for.** Growing mid-market finance teams that want approachable collections automation with a payment portal.


**Keep in mind.** It is now one line in Quadient's broader portfolio, so roadmap and support focus may be split across a larger parent.


### **8. Gaviti, Best for Fast-to-Deploy Collections Workflows**


Gaviti is a collections-first SaaS tool: configurable dunning sequences, collector task workflows, AR aging dashboards, and dispute tracking that deploy quickly on top of your existing ERP. It[raised a $9M Series A in 2022 led by Flashpoint](https://venturebeat.com/business/gaviti-raises-9m-for-saas-collections-automation) .


**Best for.** SMB and mid-market teams that want a focused, quick-to-deploy collections tool.


**Keep in mind.** It is a focused collections and analytics layer, not a full order-to-cash suite, so cash application and payments are lighter than the larger platforms.


*Also worth a look:* Chaser and Upflow are solid B2B collections tools that skew toward smaller finance teams and SMBs, worth a look if the eight above are heavier than you need.


## **Types of collections software**


"Collections software" covers several overlapping jobs, and the right tool depends on where your receivables get stuck. The main types:


- **Dunning and reminder automation** sends scheduled payment reminders and escalations so no overdue invoice is forgotten.
- **Collections workflow and worklist tools** give collectors a prioritized queue, task management, and promise-to-pay tracking.
- **Collaborative AR portals** give customers a place to view invoices, raise disputes, and pay, reducing back-and-forth.
- **Order-to-cash suites** bundle collections with credit, invoicing, and[cash application](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/cash-application) across the full cycle.
- **AI agents** go beyond managing the process and actually perform the follow-up and payment matching.


## **Which collections software is right for you?**


There is no single best collections software, only the best fit for your receivables, your customers, and your team.


- **Choose Concourse** if you want AI agents to *perform* AR follow-up and payment matching end to end, with every action traceable.
- **Choose HighRadius** if you are a large enterprise that wants autonomous, AI-driven collections at scale.
- **Choose Billtrust** if you want collections alongside invoicing and a B2B payments network.
- **Choose Versapay** if your bottleneck is customer communication and dispute resolution.
- **Choose Esker or Sidetrade** if you want collections inside a broad, AI-driven order-to-cash suite.
- **Choose Quadient AR** if you are a growing mid-market team that wants approachable automation with a payment portal.
- **Choose Gaviti** if you want a focused, fast-to-deploy collections tool.


The clearest shift in 2026 is between tools that give you a better place to *manage* collections and AI agents that *perform* the follow-up themselves. Most of this list is the former; the AI-agent layer is the latter.


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is the best collections software?**


It depends on your size and receivables. HighRadius leads for enterprise autonomous collections, Billtrust for collections tied to invoicing and payments, Versapay for collaborative customer-facing AR, and Gaviti for fast-to-deploy mid-market workflows. For teams that want AI agents to actually perform the follow-up and payment matching with full traceability, Concourse is the strongest AI-agent option.


### **What does collections software do?**


Collections software automates accounts-receivable follow-up: sequencing payment reminders and escalations, prioritizing which overdue accounts to work first, giving collectors a worklist, tracking disputes and promises to pay, and reporting on AR aging, so a team collects more cash with less manual chasing.


### **How is an AI agent different from collections software?**


Traditional collections software gives a team a place to manage follow-up: it automates reminder sequences and tracks tasks and disputes. An AI agent platform like Concourse performs the follow-up itself, drafting and sending reminders, prioritizing accounts, and matching payments across your systems, with a human approving. One manages the process; the other does the work.


### **What is the difference between collections and cash application software?**


Collections software chases overdue invoices and manages customer follow-up to bring cash in.[Cash application](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/cash-application) handles the next step: matching the payments that arrive to the right open invoices. Many order-to-cash suites, and AI agents like Concourse, cover both.


## **The bottom line**


Collections software ranges from enterprise autonomous-receivables suites to collaborative AR portals to focused workflow tools, and the right one depends on your receivables volume, your customer relationships, and your team. HighRadius and Billtrust anchor the enterprise, Versapay and Sidetrade bring collaboration and intelligence, and Gaviti serves the fast-moving mid-market.


The bigger shift is from software that helps you manage collections to software that performs them. If you want to see what AI agents can do across AR follow-up and payment matching, with every action traceable and audit-ready,[book a demo of Concourse](https://www.concourse.ai/) and put an agent on your receivables.
